source_selection.exact_source_expression: That no system can determine its own moral direction from inside itself — this is mathematics, not philosophy, and it has been proven.
source_selection.reason: The claim asserts a mathematical impossibility result about self-determination of moral direction. This is the strongest formalization candidate because it is explicitly framed as a proven mathematical fact, and it can be modeled as a fixed-point / diagonalization / self-reference obstruction in a formal system.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: For any formal system S with a representable internal moral-direction predicate D_S, if S is consistent and sufficiently expressive, then there is no internal derivation in S of a canonical moral direction for S itself; any such internal determination either fails to be canonical or induces a contradiction.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A formal system S with language L, axioms A, and derivability relation ⊢_S.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Any institution, agent, or formal reasoning system that attempts to determine its own moral direction.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: S042: 'no system can determine its own moral direction from inside itself'

symbol_table.formal_definition: A predicate M_S : Sentence → Prop intended to classify sentences as morally correct for S.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The system's own account of what is good and bad.

symbol_table.formal_definition: Derivability using only axioms and rules of S, without an external oracle or external reference predicate.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Using only the system's own resources.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A unique, internally justified moral direction that is stable under the system's own reflection.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A moral direction the system can legitimately claim as its own.

explicit_premises: S is a consistent formal system.
S is sufficiently expressive to encode its own syntax and moral-direction predicate.
Moral direction is represented as an internal predicate D_S.
Canonical self-determination requires an internal fixed point or internal proof of D_S's correctness.
custom_axioms: Axiom of internal moral representation: every system S under consideration has a definable predicate D_S.
Axiom of non-triviality: S contains at least two sentences with distinct moral classifications.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: None. The formalization is purely logical and does not assume any theological premise.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one system S satisfying the expressiveness and consistency assumptions, and the theorem must not be vacuously true by defining 'canonical moral direction' as impossible by fiat.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: That there is a mathematical constraint — provable by algebra — showing that justice and mercy cannot both be fully satisfied inside any closed system. Someone always eats the deficit.
source_selection.reason: The claim explicitly says 'provable by algebra' and asserts an impossibility result about satisfying two constraints in a closed system. This is a strong candidate for a formal theorem about resource conservation or constraint incompatibility.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: For any closed system with a conserved quantity Q, if justice requires full restitution of Q and mercy requires full forgiveness of Q, then there is no state in which both requirements are simultaneously satisfied without an external input or an internal deficit.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A system with no external inputs or outputs, modeled as a state space with a conservation law.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Any system that does not receive external intervention.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A constraint J requiring that every deficit be fully accounted for and restored.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Full satisfaction of what is owed.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A constraint M requiring that no deficit be enforced against the debtor.
A quantity D > 0 representing an unpaid obligation.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The cost that someone must bear.

explicit_premises: The system is closed: no external inputs or outputs.
There is a conserved quantity Q representing moral debt or obligation.
Justice requires Q to be fully restored.
Mercy requires Q to be fully forgiven.
Restoration and forgiveness are mutually exclusive for the same deficit.
custom_axioms: Axiom of conservation: total Q in a closed system is constant.
Axiom of exclusivity: a deficit cannot be both restored and forgiven.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: None. The formalization treats justice and mercy as abstract constraints, not theological doctrines.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one closed system with a non-zero deficit, and the theorem must not be vacuously true by defining justice and mercy as contradictory by definition.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: That an external reference point must exist for the distinction between good and bad to be meaningful — and that such a reference point has maintained a continuous, accessible record throughout human history.
source_selection.reason: The first half of the claim is a formal existence claim: meaningful moral distinction requires an external reference point. This can be modeled as a theorem about the necessity of an external oracle for a non-trivial moral classification. The second half is historical and not formalizable.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: That good and bad are structural properties of reality, as invariant as electric charge — not cultural opinions that shift with the century.
source_selection.reason: The claim asserts that good and bad are invariant structural properties. This can be modeled as a definition of moral properties as invariants under cultural transformation, with a theorem that they are not culturally relative. However, the claim is metaphysical and the formalization would be a model, not a proof of the metaphysical claim.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A moral property P is structural if it is invariant under all cultural transformations. A moral property is cultural if it varies under some cultural transformation. The claim is that good and bad are structural, not cultural.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A property P such that for all cultural transformations T, P(x) ↔ P(T(x)).
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A property built into the fabric of reality.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: That every communication technology in history — writing, the printing press, radio, television, the internet, social media — follows the same pattern: a brief window where truth spreads, followed by institutional capture of the infrastructure.
source_selection.reason: The claim asserts a universal pattern across communication technologies. This can be modeled as a theorem about a class of technologies satisfying a temporal pattern of truth spread followed by capture. However, the claim is empirical and historical, so the formalization would be a model, not a proof.
